influences.name: Primal Scream
influences.context: Homem-Christo referred to Screamadelica by Primal Scream as the record that "put everything together" in terms of genre.

influences.name: Andy Warhol
influences.context: In 2009, Bangalter named Andy Warhol as one of Daft Punk's early influences.

influences.name: Paul Johnson

influences.name: Romanthony
influences.context: On the Homework track "Teachers", Daft Punk list musicians who influenced them, including Chicago house and Detroit techno artists including Romanthony and Todd Edwards. Homem-Christo said: "Their music had a big effect on us. The sound of their productions—the compression, the sound of the kick drum and Romanthony's voice, the emotion and soul—is part of how we sound today."

influences.name: Todd Edwards
influences.context: On the Homework track "Teachers", Daft Punk list musicians who influenced them, including Chicago house and Detroit techno artists including Paul Johnson, Romanthony and Todd Edwards. Homem-Christo said: "Their music had a big effect on us."

influences.name: Aphex Twin
influences.context: A major inspiration was the 1999 Aphex Twin single "Windowlicker", which Bangalter said was "neither a purely club track nor a very chilled-out, down-tempo relaxation track".

influences.name: Supertramp
influences.context: Daft Punk also used vintage equipment to recreate sounds by older artists, such as the use of a Wurlitzer piano to evoke Supertramp on "Digital Love".

influences.name: Stanley Kubrick
influences.context: 2001: A Space Odyssey is maybe my favourite film and the way [Stanley] Kubrick presented it is so relevant today - because he is asking exactly the question that we have to ask ourselves about technology and the obsolescence of man.
